newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end one percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end one percent higher.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares closed one percent higher after a firming Wall Street supported the indices in late trade.

The easing Swiss franc was favourable for industrials, dealers said. A techical reaction to Friday's losses buoyed shares from the start, but some profit taking temporarily put prices under pressure. "People do not want to take chances ahead of the year's end", a trader noted. Volumes sagged towards the end of the session.
Further development was seen depending on Wall Street.
* Blue-chip up 38.5 points, or one percent, to 3,874.0.

* On the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex), volatilities and volumes were below those of last Friday, when trade was dominated by shockwaves from U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks about "irrational exuberance" on asset markets.
In total, 102,851 options were trade with a call put ration vo 1.68 to one. 35,035 SMI options changed hands.
On the futures side, 6,526 SMI futures contracts were traded. The December SMI futures added 46 points to 3,872.
